chapter_name: Chapter 09: Use of Is, Am, Are
learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will learn the rules of helping verbs: matching 'Am' with I, 'Is' with singular words, and 'Are' with plural words.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Meet the three best friends of the grammar world: Is, Am, and Are! They are Helping Verbs, but they are very picky about who they hold hands with. Let's learn their rules!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Is, Am, and Are do not show action like running or jumping. Instead, they help complete the sentence and tell us about 'now' (present time).
'Am' has only ONE best friend in the whole world. It ONLY holds hands with the pronoun 'I'.
We use 'Is' when we talk about ONE person, animal, or thing. It holds hands with He, She, It, and Singular Nouns.
We use 'Are' when we talk about MANY people or things. It holds hands with We, They, Plural Nouns, and also the special word 'You'!

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ The children ____ playing in the park.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank: She ____ my best friend.
subjective_practice.hint: She is only one girl. Which helping verb do we use for singular? (Is / Are)

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Choose the correct word: You (is / are) very kind.
subjective_practice.hint: Remember the special rule for 'You'. It always takes the plural helping verb!

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank: Rahul and Amit ____ going to school.
subjective_practice.hint: Rahul and Amit makes TWO people. Which helping verb is for many? (Are)

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎨 The 'Is, Am, Are' Family Tree
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Draw three big branches of a tree. Label them IS, AM, and ARE. Draw leaves on the 'AM' branch and write 'I'. On the 'IS' branch write He, She, It. On 'ARE' write We, You, They!

chapter_summary: ⭐ 'Is' is used with Singular words like He, She, It.
⭐ 'Are' is used with Plural words like We, They, and the special word You.
